annotations.text:
The tile glyph: pick one (or pair them).
My lean: A (rings) at kid size on My Sounds, B (split ring) small in dense teacher grids (44px wherever it's tappable), C (ink bars) wherever it prints. Same data behind all three.

Generated per child, per level: exact bookmark colour, gold stars from their real mastery, QR plays this set's sounds spliced from the phoneme recordings.
Graphemes here are Georgia stand-ins — the real print renders from the Vic-cursive stroke paths, no font licence needed.

The mystery counter is the key move: a kid who answers chip–counter–typed for 'sheep' has PROVEN 3-sound segmentation even though /ee/ is beyond them. Counting credit and spelling credit are scored separately — the counter never counts against them, and each revealed mystery offers its sound as the next thing to learn.

Progress display = home screen = task router. Each open ring on the expanded tile deep-links into the task that closes it (read → flashcards, spell → Listen & Write, write → Handwriting). The bookmark shelf is the long-game view; a finished level earns the printed bookmark.

The front door: Reading (letters→sounds) and Spelling (sounds→letters) as the two big rooms, Handwriting as its own strip. Each room = its wall view + its practice tasks + its skills. The ring hues carry through: blue reading, purple spelling, green handwriting.

Works for ANY scope & sequence: programs are stored as orderings of grapheme–sound pairs, and both walls are derived views (already live in the Explorer for all 7 programs). Rules attach to spellings, not programs — Magic e appears whenever a-e gets taught, in any sequence, and locked rules say which unit unlocks them.
